name: Turnip
grown_as: The garden turnip, a biennial grown as an annual for its white root, drawn as a white globe with a purple top like 'Purple Top Milan'. Some varieties are all white ('Snowball') or yellow-fleshed ('Golden Ball'). ⚠️ CHECK: William's variety.
habit: Year 1: an upright rosette of leaves 25 to 40 cm high from the top of a round root that sits half above the soil. Year 2: a branched flowering stem 50 to 100 cm, its upper leaves clasping the stem.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette from the top of the root; alternate on the flowering stem
leaf.type: Simple, deeply lobed: lyre-shaped (lyrate), a large rounded end lobe and 2 to 4 pairs of smaller side lobes on the lower part
leaf.outline: Long oblong, 20 to 40 cm, widest near the tip
leaf.base: Tapering into the stalk, small lobes along it. Upper stem leaves undivided, clasping the stem with two rounded ear-like lobes
leaf.margin: Wavy and irregularly, bluntly toothed all round
leaf.veins: A broad pale midrib with netted side veins
leaf.surface: Rough with stiff bristly hairs, especially on the young leaves and stalks; NOT waxy

flower.petals: Four, free, oval on short claws, in a cross
flower.centre: Six stamens (four long, two short) round a green style
flower.behind: Four narrow green-yellow sepals spreading or held out from the petals
flower.carried: In a flat-topped cluster at the tip of each branch, the open flowers standing ABOVE the unopened buds; the spike lengthens as pods form below
flower.season: March to May of the second year

fruit: Slender cylindrical pods 4 to 7 cm long, with a thin beak 1 to 2 cm, held up on spreading stalks; they split lengthwise to release small round dark red-brown to black seeds.
seedling: Two kidney- to heart-shaped seed leaves, notched at the tip, on short stalks, bright green; the first true leaves rough-hairy, oval and toothed.
winter: Roots lifted in autumn or left in the ground in mild spells; tops die back in hard frost. Spring greens (turnip tops) come from roots left in.

leaf: lyre-shaped with a large rounded end lobe and smaller side lobes below
bristly-hairy and grass green, not waxy grey
bloom: four bright yellow petals in a cross
open flowers held above the buds at the cluster tip
seed: a tiny round dark red-brown to black seed, about 1.5 mm
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip
young: a rosette of rough lobed green leaves
a white root starting to swell at the soil
crop: a round, slightly flattened root sitting half out of the soil
white below, purple where it was in the light above the soil
no neck: leaves rise straight from the top
flower: a branched stem with clasping upper leaves
bright yellow cross-shaped flowers in flat-topped clusters
seedhead: slender upright beaked pods along the stems

look_alikes: Swede has smooth, waxy, grey-green leaves, a neck of leaf scars on the root and yellow flesh; its buds stand above its open flowers. Kohlrabi is a swollen stem above ground with leaves rising from its sides. Radish has a smaller root and pale lilac flowers. Oilseed rape is like a swede, not a turnip.
